title: Fix 'zsh: command not found: brew' after installing Homebrew
summary: Homebrew is installed, but the Terminal does not yet know where the brew program is. Adding Homebrew's setup line to your zsh profile makes brew work in new Terminal windows.

aliases.text: command not found brew after install
homebrew installed but brew not found
brew not working in new terminal
команда brew не найдена на mac
homebrew установлен но brew не работает
brew не работает в новом терминале
как сделать чтобы brew работал в терминале

prerequisites: Homebrew was installed with the official installer, so the brew program exists in /opt/homebrew (Apple Silicon) or /usr/local (Intel)

steps.explain: Find out where Homebrew is installed. On Apple Silicon Macs it is in /opt/homebrew, on Intel Macs in /usr/local. The command only lists files and changes nothing.
Check whether your zsh profile already has a Homebrew line. No output means the line is missing, so the next step is needed. The command only reads the file.
Add Homebrew's setup line to the end of ~/.zprofile. zsh reads this file when a new Terminal window opens, and the line puts brew on your PATH. Run it only once, or the line will be added twice.

alternatives.explain: Use this line instead on an Intel Mac, where Homebrew is in /usr/local.

steps.explain: Load the updated profile into the current Terminal window, so brew works here without opening a new window.

verify.expect: Prints /opt/homebrew/bin/brew on Apple Silicon or /usr/local/bin/brew on Intel. Nothing printed means brew is still not on the PATH.
Prints a line starting with Homebrew and a version number, for example Homebrew 4.x.
